newsitem.title: USA: US Fed likely to raise rates -- ex-Fed Gov Angell.
newsitem.headline: US Fed likely to raise rates -- ex-Fed Gov Angell.

text.p: Former Federal Reserve Governor Wayne Angell said Thursday the Fed was likely to raise interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point next week.
The Fed's policymaking Federal Open Market Committee is scheduled to meet March 25.
Angell said he expected Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan would make a recommendation "to raise rates a quarter of a point" and other Fed policymakers would go along with that at the meeting.
Last month, Angell had said he expected the central bank to keep interest rates steady as inflation was not expected to accelerate.
Angell spoke to reporters after listening to Greenspan's testimony before the congressional Joint Economic Committee. He said he found Greenspan's use of the word "promptly" significant.
In his testimony, Greenspan stressed "the importance of acting promptly -- ideally pre-emptively -- to keep inflation low over the intermediate term and to promote price stability over time."
